text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock rose 0.33% today to $423.37, continuing a sharp nine-day rally that's gained 6.8% since mid-September. The climb reflects tightening refinery economics: US oil trades at $107 per barrel while world oil sits at $130.80—a widening gap that benefits refiners who buy cheaper domestic crude and sell into global markets. Simultaneously, US refineries are running at 96.8% capacity with diesel and heating oil inventories at their lowest levels in the data shown, supporting margins on refined products.

The broader backdrop is a Middle East supply scare that's kept energy markets elevated. While Saudi Arabia offered to increase crude supplies through the Hormuz Strait after the pipeline attack, concerns about regional escalation persist. High diesel prices are already cascading through transportation costs nationwide, which creates economic headwinds but doesn't immediately dent refiner profits—it actually pushes up what refiners can charge for their products in the near term.
